_comment: The people of the Confluence village. spot names a place in the village layout (Core/Town/Village.cs). talk lines are tried in order and the first whose 'when' holds is said; 'when' can test quest (with state none/active/done, stage, ready) and flag. Each choice can start or advance a quest and has an optional reply. A Goodbye answer is always added. All names are placeholders.

talk.say: You came up out of the ground with the hum gone quiet behind you. You woke the heart already, didn't you? Tell me.

choices.text: I woke it. The sentinel is broken.

talk.say: A stranger, with sky-dust still on you. Sit, if you like. Since you fell, the old stone to the south has been humming. The builders left a shrine there, buried. Nobody here can read their words any more.

choices.text: I'll go and see what's humming.
choices.reply: Follow the paved road south. Read what is carved before you speak; the old words answer only those who listen first.
Nobody knows. Whoever they were, they were here long before any of us, and their words still move stone.
The Teshari Confluence. Rest here whenever you need; the walls keep the night off.

talk.say: The road south leads to the arch. Read the carvings with care, and when a word comes to you, speak it where the stone can hear.

choices.text: How do I speak a word?
choices.reply: Say it toward the thing you mean it for. (Press X, pick the word with its number, then Enter.)

talk.say: The hum has stopped. You went all the way down, didn't you?

choices.text: The heart fell. It said: the world remembers.
choices.reply: I don't know what that means. Nobody does. But the hum has stopped, and you came back. Keep these, for the road.

talk.say: The old stone to the south is quiet now. You did that. The village is yours as much as ours.
Hungry? Everyone's hungry. The redstriders came close to the village this season, but nobody has had time to hunt. Bring me four cuts of raw meat and I'll make it worth your while.

choices.reply: Strike from the side, not the front. And mind the herd: if one runs, they all do.
Wonderful. Take some back, cooked properly, and a fire kit for the road.

talk.say: Four cuts of raw meat, friend. The redstriders graze the grass just outside the village.
The hearth's never been so full. Come by when you're hungry.
Something walks the grass at night: big, quiet, all teeth. I'm out of arrowheads. Eight pieces of flint and I can watch for it properly.

choices.reply: Grey nodules, on rocky ground. You can pick them up by hand.

talk.say: Is that flint I hear clacking in your bag?

choices.reply: Good stone. Here, a pick of my own making. Rock gives way to it.

talk.say: Eight pieces of flint. Grey nodules on rocky ground.
You've a good eye for stone. There's a steading past the wall, south-east, off the ruin road. Empty as long as I've kept the watch. The carved stone in its yard held a Tether once.

choices.text: Could I make it my home?
choices.reply: Set a new Tether on that stone and it's yours. Walls need mending, mind.

talk.say: I saw the light take, out past the wall. So the old place has someone again.

choices.reply: Then you'll want to mend it. Take this stone and timber; I won't be needing it.

talk.say: The steading's south-east, past the wall. Set a Tether on the carved stone in the yard.
Quiet night so far. If you see eyes in the grass, come back to the fire.
You went down to the heart, didn't you? Tell me everything you saw. Every carving, every word. I will write it down.

choices.reply: Each ring is one word, copied as the builders carved it. Read the same words in the ruins and they will start to mean something to you.

talk.say: Quietly, please. This is the Grand College library. Everything we know of the builders' words is on these shelves, and most of it we cannot read.

choices.reply: Each ring is one word, copied as the builders carved it. Read the same words in the ruins and they will start to mean something to you.

choices.text: Can you teach me the words?
choices.reply: Nobody teaches them. You read them where they were carved, in two different places, and then you try them. The elder at the Confluence will tell you where to start.
